Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:1.hebrew: פטרוה לא אמר כלום - דדלמא לשון פטור וחובה, להקל מעליה חובות שחייבת:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:1.english: [If he said,] "Release her," he has said nothing - for perhaps [it is] an expression of release [from] obligation, [meaning] to relieve her of debts that she owes:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:2.hebrew: פרנסוה - כל לשון פרנסה, לשון עשיית צרכיה הוא, קונדיי"ר בלע"ז, כמו "לפרנסה שמין באב" (כתובות דף סח.), וכמו "מוציאין לפרנסה ואין מוציאין למזונות" (שם דף סט.). הלכך, לא ידעינן אי צורכי גט הוא שלא תהא זקוקה ליבם, או צורכי מלבוש וכסות הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:2.english: Sustain her - Every expression of parnasah [provision] is an expression of attending to her needs — conreier [to equip/provide for] in Old French — as in "for parnasah [dowry] we assess the father['s means]" (Ketubot 68a), and as in "we extract [funds] for parnasah [dowry], but we do not extract for sustenance" (ibid. 69a). Therefore, we do not know whether he means the needs of a bill of divorce [get], so that she will not be bound to a yavam [brother-in-law], or [whether] he means the needs of clothing and garments:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:3.hebrew: כנימוס - כחוק; לא ידעינן אי חק גט אי חק מזון וכסות, וכן "כראוי":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:10:3.english: According to the law [kenimus] - [This means] according to the statute; we do not know whether [he meant] the statute of a bill of divorce or the statute of food and clothing. And similarly [for] "appropriately":

Rashi on Gittin 65b:11:1.hebrew: שלחוה - לשון "ושלחה מביתו" (דברים כ״ד:א׳) נקט האי גברא:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:11:1.english: Send her - This man used the expression "and he sends her out of his house" (Deuteronomy 24:1):

Rashi on Gittin 65b:11:2.english: Release her [shevukuha] - [This is] the language of a bill of release [iggeret shevukin]:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:11:3.english: Banish her - An expression of banishment [terukhin], [meaning] divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:1.hebrew: ר' נתן אומר פיטרוה דבריו קיימין - לשון גט פטורין, כך שמעתי. ולי נראה הפוך: "פטרוה", שעל כרחך בלשון צואה הוא, כמו "שלחוה", וכמו "דברו", "שברו", הוא לשון גט פטורין, שהוא דגש. "פיטרוה", שבלשון צוואה הוא רפי, כמו "אמרו", "שלחו מכם" (בראשית מ״ב:ט״ז), "שמעו מלכים" (שופטים ה׳:ג׳), אף "פיטרוה" הוא לשון פטור וחובה, דאי לשון פטורין, היה לו להדגיש "פטרוה":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:1.english: Rabbi Natan says: Pitruha, his statement stands - [This means it is] an expression of a bill of release [get piturin]; thus have I heard. But to me it appears the opposite: Patruha, which perforce is in the imperative form — like shilchuha ["send her"], and like dabru ["speak"] [and] shabru ["break"] — is the expression of a bill of release, as it has a dagesh. [By contrast,] pitruha, which in the imperative form is soft [i.e., without a dagesh] — like imru ["say"], shilchu mikem ["send of you"] (Genesis 42:16), [and] shimu melachim ["hear, O kings"] (Judges 5:3) — pitruha too is an expression of exemption and obligation [i.e., "exempt her"], for if [it meant] an expression of release [from marriage], it should have had a dagesh: patruha.

Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:2.hebrew: רבי נתן דבבלאה הוא - שבא מבבל, כדאמרינן בבבא בתרא (דף קלא.): "והעזתי פני בנתן הבבלי":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:2.english: Rabbi Natan, who is a Babylonian - [meaning] that he came from Babylonia, as we say in Bava Batra (131a): "I acted brazenly toward Natan the Babylonian":

Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:3.hebrew: ודייק בין פיטרוה לפטרוה - שמספרין פעמים בלשון ארמי ופעמים בלשון עברי, הלכך כי אמר "פטרוה", לשון גט פטורין הוא, שהדגיש וסיפר בלשון ארמי; וכי אמר "פיטרוה", סיפר בלשון עברי ואמר לשון פטור וחובה:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:3.english: And he distinguishes between pitruha and patruha - For [the Babylonians] speak sometimes in the Aramaic language and sometimes in the Hebrew language; therefore, when he said "patruha," it is an expression of a bill of release [get piturin, i.e., divorce], for he emphasized [its pronunciation] and spoke in the Aramaic language; and when he said "pitruha," he spoke in the Hebrew language and used an expression of exemption and obligation.

Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:4.hebrew: תנא דידן דבר ארעא דישראל הוא - וכל סיפורו לשון עברי, לא דייק בין "פטרוה" ובין "פיטרוה", ולאו לגט פיטורין איכוון, דפיטורין לשון ארמי הוא, תרגום של "שילוח":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:12:4.english: The Tanna of our [Mishnah], who is a resident of the Land of Israel - and all his speech is [in] the Hebrew language, does not distinguish between "patruha" and "pitruha", and [holds that] he did not intend a bill of divorce [get pitturin], for "pitturin" is an Aramaic term, the translation [Targum] of "shiluach" [sending away]:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:1.hebrew: הוציאוה מהו - מי אמרי' לישנא דקרא נקט, "ויצאה מביתו" (דברים כ״ד:ב׳), או דילמא לאו לישנא דקרא הוא, דלא כתיב "והוציאה מביתו", אלא "ויצאה" — היא מעצמה:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:1.english: [If he said:] "Remove her," what is [the halakha]? - Do we say [that] he used the language of the verse, "and she goes out of his house" (Deuteronomy 24:2), or perhaps it is not the language of the verse, for it is not written "and he removed her from his house," rather "and she goes out" — [meaning] she [goes out] on her own:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:2.hebrew: עזבוה מהו - לשון איגרת שיבוקין הוא, או דלמא כיון דלאו לשון עזיבה כתבינן בגט, לאו לישנא דגיטא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:2.english: "Abandon her," what is [the halakha] - [Is it that] it is an expression of "a bill of release" [iggeret shivukin], or perhaps, since we do not write an expression of "abandoning" in a get, it is not an expression [valid] for a get?

Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:3.hebrew: התירוה מהו - לשון "מותרת לכל אדם" הוא, או לשון התרת נדרים או התרת חגורה:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:13:3.english: Unbind her, what is [the halakha] - Is it an expression of [being] permitted to any man, or an expression of annulling vows, or untying a belt?

Rashi on Gittin 65b:14:1.hebrew: פשוט מיהא - מתניתא פושטת חדא מהני בעיין: "עשו לה כדת", לא אמר כלום:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:14:1.english: Resolve at least - [A] baraita [resolves] one of these dilemmas: "Treat her according to the custom" — he has said nothing:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:1.english: One who goes out in a neck chain - to be executed by the government:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:2.hebrew: ואמר כתבו - אע"פ שלא אמר תנו:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:2.english: And [he] said, "Write" - Even though he did not say, "Give":

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:3.english: They should write and give [it] - For because of his fear he is preoccupied and did not specify [to give it]:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:4.english: One who sets out - to sea:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:5.english: And one who departs in a caravan - to the deserts:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:15:6.english: One who is dangerously ill - a sick person:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:16:1.english: From wine - from the wine that I have:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:2:1.hebrew: דהא מראה מקום היא לו - דאמר רבי אלעזר לעיל: אשה, כיון דלאו בדידה תליא, קביעות מקומה לא הויא קפידא, אלא כמראה מקום:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:2:1.english: As she is indicating a place for him - For Rabbi Elazar said above: [Regarding] a woman, since [the divorce] does not depend on her, her specification of a place is not [a strict] stipulation, but rather like indicating a place:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:3:1.hebrew: לא צריכא - הא דאיצטריך למיתני "אוסר מיד", אלא דאיתיה לבעל במזרח, והאי שליח אזיל למערב:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:3:1.english: No, it is necessary - [that is,] that which it was necessary to teach, "[it] prohibits immediately," [is] only where the husband is in the east, and this agent is going to the west:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:3:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא - לא תתסר מיד, דהא למערב ליתיה לבעל, דניחוש דלמא משכח ליה באורחיה בצאתו מן העיר:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:3:2.english: Lest you say - she does not become forbidden immediately, for the husband is not in the west that we should be concerned lest [the agent] find him on his way as he leaves the city:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:3:3.english: He encounters him - [meaning] he chances upon him:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:4:1.english: Establish an eiruv for me with dates - [place it] at the end of the two thousand [cubits] of the [Shabbat] boundary:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:5:1.hebrew: הא רבנן - דאמרי לעיל גבי דידה, אע"ג דלא בדידה תליא ולא איכפת לה, אמרי': כל מאי דאמר איניש לשלוחיה אי שני לאו שלוחיה הוא; ה"נ אין עירובו עירוב:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:5:1.english: This [baraita is in accordance with] the Rabbis - who said earlier regarding her [case]: Even though it does not depend on her and she does not care, we say that [for] anything a person tells his agent, if he deviates, he is not his agent; so too here, his eiruv is not [a valid] eiruv:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:5:2.english: He is [merely] indicating a place for him - in a matter where there is no loss and he does not mind:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:6:1.hebrew: הא והא רבנן - ואינהו נמי לא אמור קפידא אלא גבי אשה, דהתם ניחא ליה דתיתזל ולאו בדוכתא אחרינא; והנך מתנייתא — כאן בשלו, עירובו עירוב, דלא איכפת ליה, והאי דקתני "אינו עירוב", כגון דיהב ליה חבריה רשות לערובי מתמרים דידיה, ואמר לו האיך לשלוחיה: "ערב לי בתמרים דפלוני", דהכא ודאי קפידא הוא, דבגרוגרות דחבריה לית ליה רשותא:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:6:1.english: Both this and that [are the opinion of] the Rabbis - And they too only stated [that there is] insistence regarding a wife, for there he wants her to be degraded [in that specific place], and not in another place; and [regarding] those baraitot: "here, with his own [produce]" — his eiruv is a [valid] eiruv, for he does not care; and that [baraita] which teaches "it is not a [valid] eiruv" — [is speaking of a case] such as where his fellow gave him permission to make an eiruv from his [fellow's] dates, and that one said to his agent: "Make an eiruv for me with the dates of so-and-so," for here there is certainly insistence, since he does not have permission [to use] his fellow's dried figs:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:7:1.hebrew: במגדל - קא סלקא דעתין: "הנח לי עירובי במגדל שבסוף אלפים":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:7:1.english: In a tower - We initially assumed [that he meant], "Place my eiruv for me in a tower that is at the end of two thousand [cubits]."

Rashi on Gittin 65b:7:2.hebrew: מאי שלו ומאי של חבירו איכא - דמקפיד? מי מקפיד ההוא חבריה אי מנח ליה בהאי או בהאי:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:7:2.english: What [distinction between] his and another's is there - that he would be particular? Would that other person be particular whether he places it in this [one] or in that [one]:

Rashi on Gittin 65b:8:1.hebrew: פירי דמגדל - "במגדל" דקתני, לאו לאתנוחיה הוא, אלא: ערב לי מפירות פלוני שיש לו במגדל:
Rashi on Gittin 65b:8:1.english: Fruit of the tower - [The phrase] "in the tower" that [the baraita] teaches does not refer to placing [the eiruv there]; rather, [he meant]: "Make an eiruv for me from the produce of So-and-so that he has in the tower":

Rashi on Gittin 65b:9:1.hebrew: כתבו גט ותנו לאשתי - לשון בני אדם הוא, כבר החזיקו בו לקרות לספר כריתות אשה "גט":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:9:1.english: Write a get [bill of divorce] and give [it] to my wife - This is common parlance; [people] have already adopted [the practice] of calling a woman's bill of divorce [sefer keritut] a "get":

Rashi on Gittin 65b:9:2.english: Divorce her - [This] too [is common usage, as people] have already become accustomed to call [the giving of a bill of divorce] "divorce."

Rashi on Gittin 65b:9:3.hebrew: כתבו איגרת ותנו לה - גם זה לשון הגט, שכותבין בו "ודן דיהוי ליכי מינאי ספר תירוכין ואיגרת שבוקין":
Rashi on Gittin 65b:9:3.english: Write a letter and give [it] to her - This too is the wording of a bill of divorce, for one writes in it: "And this shall be to you from me a document of dismissal and a letter of release":

Tosafot on Gittin 65b:1:1.hebrew: גיטא לא הוי עד דמטית למתא מחסיא - וא"ת: ואם אינה רוצה שיהא גט עד מתא מחסיא, גם כשיגיע למתא מחסיא לא יהא גט, דהא אינו מקבלו שם מיד הבעל, והוי כמו "טלי גט מעל גבי קרקע"! ואי מיירי כשהבעל עושהו שליח להולכה עד מתא מחסיא, ושם הוי שליח לקבלה — והא לא חזרה שליחות אצל הבעל! וי"ל, דמיירי דא"ל: הוי שליח להולכה עד דמטית התם, וכי מטית התם שוי שליח להולכה וקבליה, כדאמרי' בפ' שני (לעיל גיטין דף כד.). א"נ, מבבל ועד מתא מחסיא הוי הכל שליח לקבלה, והוי כאומר לאשה: ה"ז גיטך, ולא תתגרשי בו עד לאחר ל' יום. רבינו יצחק ב"ר מאיר:
Tosafot on Gittin 65b:1:1.english: It is not a bill of divorce until you reach Mata Meḥasya - And if you ask: If she does not want it to be a bill of divorce until Mata Meḥasya, then even when he reaches Mata Meḥasya it should not be a bill of divorce, since he does not receive it there from the hand of the husband, and it is like [a husband saying to his wife], "Take [your] bill of divorce from upon the ground"! And if [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where the husband makes him an agent for delivery until Mata Meḥasya, and there he becomes an agent for receipt — [even so,] the agency has not returned to the husband! And one can answer: [The Gemara] is speaking of a case where [the husband] said to him: "Be an agent for delivery until you reach there, and when you reach there, appoint an agent for delivery and receive it [from him]," as we say in the second chapter (above, Gittin 24a). Alternatively, from Babylon until Mata Meḥasya it is all [an agency of] an agent for receipt, and it is like one who says to a woman: "Here is your bill of divorce, and you shall not be divorced by it until after thirty days." [So explained] Rabbeinu Yitzḥak ben Rabbi Meir:

Tosafot on Gittin 65b:6:1.hebrew: הא והא רבנן - פי' בקונטרס דלרבנן נמי לא הוי קפידא אלא גבי אשה, משום דהתם ניחא ליה דתיתזיל ולא בדוכתא אחרינא, אבל גבי עירוב בשלו לא איכפת ליה. והא דקתני "אינו עירוב" בשל חבירו, כגון דיהיב ליה חבריה רשותא לערב בתמרים דידיה, דהכא ודאי קפידא הויא, דבגרוגרות דחבריה לית ליה רשותא. וקשה, דלא משמע כלל דפליג רב יוסף אסוגיא דלעיל, דסבר דלרבנן הוי קפידא בעירוב שלו כמו באשה, ולא בא רב יוסף לחדש אלא בשל חבירו. ועוד, דא"כ, הל"ל "הא והא ככולי עלמא", דרבי אלעזר נמי מודה בשל חבירו דהויא קפידא, כמו בבעל דמודה ר"א דהוי קפידא. ולכך נראה לפרש דשלו הוי קפידא, אבל בשל חבירו — דהוי בשל שליח — בכל מה שירצה השליח יערב לו, כיון דמערב לו בפירותיו. וא"ת: השתא משמע דלרבנן בשלו הוי קפידא גם לרב יוסף כדפירשנו, וכן בפ' (הנהנה) [השליח] (מעילה דף כא.): "הבא לי מן החלון", והביא לו מן הדלוסקמא, שליח מעל, משום דלא עשה שליח שליחותו דקפידא הוי; ותימה דבסוף המפקיד (ב"מ דף מב:) גבי כשותא משמע דלא הוי קפידא, משום דלא אמר לו "מהאי רמי ומהאי לא רמי"! ואין נראה לומר דאתיא לרבי אלעזר דהכא — דהילכתא כוותיה, דקאי רשב"ג בשיטתיה בפ' גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסה.) — מדלא מייתי לה התם בהמפקיד. ונראה דהכא ודאי שהזכיר תמרים וגרוגרות, והזכיר חלון ודלוסקמא, לא היה מזכיר אם לא שהיה מקפיד; אבל בהמפקיד, דאחוי לסרסיה היכן כשות שלו מונח, והוו התם תרי כריא דכשותא, וגם אין רגילין להקפיד כיון שהכל מין אחד, הא לא הוי ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה שיהא לאחרים כשות בביתו של זה:
Tosafot on Gittin 65b:6:1.english: Both this and that are the Rabbis - Rashi explained that even according to the Rabbis, there is insistence only with regard to [betrothing] a woman, because there he is amenable to her being demeaned [in one place] and not in another place; however, regarding an eiruv with his own [produce], he does not care. And that which [the baraita] teaches, "it is not an eiruv," [which Rav Yosef explains as referring to] that of another person, is a case where his fellow gave him permission to make an eiruv with his dates — for here there certainly is insistence, as he does not have permission [to use] his fellow's dried figs. And this is difficult, for it does not seem at all that Rav Yosef disagrees with the sugya above, which holds that according to the Rabbis there is insistence regarding an eiruv with his own [produce] just as with a woman, and Rav Yosef only came to innovate regarding that of another person. Furthermore, if so [that there is no insistence with his own produce even according to the Rabbis], he should have said, "Both this and that are according to everyone," for Rabbi Elazar also agrees regarding that of another person that there is insistence, just as in [the case of] a husband, where Rabbi Elazar agrees that there is insistence. Therefore, it seems [preferable] to explain that [with] his own [produce] there is insistence; however, with that of another — meaning with the agent's own [produce] — with whatever the agent wishes he may make the eiruv for him, since he is making the eiruv for him with his [own] fruit. And if you ask: Now it is implied that according to the Rabbis, with his own [produce] there is insistence even according to Rav Yosef, as we have explained — and likewise in the chapter [entitled] (HaNeheneh) [HaShaliach] (Meilah 21a): [If one says,] "Bring me [something] from the window," and he brought it to him from the chest, the agent has committed me'ilah [misappropriation of sacred property], because the agent did not fulfill his agency, as there is insistence — and [if so,] it is astonishing that at the end of HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 42b) regarding hops, it is implied that there is no insistence, because he did not say to him, "Cast from this and do not cast from that"! And it does not seem [correct] to say that [the passage in Bava Metzia] follows Rabbi Elazar of here — whom the halakha follows, as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stands in accordance with his view in the chapter [entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 165a) — since [the Gemara] does not cite it there in HaMafkid. Rather, it seems that here, where he explicitly mentioned dates and dried figs, and [there where he] mentioned a window and a chest, he would not have mentioned [them] unless he was insistent. However, in HaMafkid, where he showed his brewer where his hops were lying, and there were two piles of hops there — and moreover, people are not accustomed to be insistent since it is all one type [of produce] — it would not have entered his mind that others would have hops in this person's house:

Tosafot on Gittin 65b:7:1.hebrew: מאי שלו ושל חבירו איכא - לא בעי לשנויי: הא דתניא "עירובו עירוב" — בסמוכין זה לזה, והא דתניא "אין עירובו עירוב" — במרוחקין זה מזה; דא"כ, אפי' שובך ושובך נמי! ועוד, דניחא ליה לשנויי הכל בחד גוונא:
Tosafot on Gittin 65b:7:1.english: What [distinction between] his and another's is there - [He] did not want to answer [that] that [baraita] which teaches "his eiruv is a [valid] eiruv" [refers to a case] where they are near one another, and that [baraita] which teaches "his eiruv is not a [valid] eiruv" [refers to a case] where they are far from one another; for if so, even [in the case of] a dovecote and a dovecote [this distinction would] also [apply]! And furthermore, [he] preferred to answer everything in the same manner:
